clauses.reason: Terminated by own terms: 'until April 1, 1937' (stated date inclusive, 1937-04-01; exclusive reading one day earlier). Actor EO:6998 itself. Later events: new 'further exemption' grants of the same person, each with its own date and quote; none revokes or amends this order.

research_rationale:
EO:6998 (1935-03-30) is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 exempting Harry O. Bailey from compulsory retirement for age and continuing the person in the service 'until April 1, 1937'. The order ends by its own terms on 1937-04-01 (stated date, inclusive; exclusive alternative one day earlier, per the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on 'until' dates). Later orders in the same person's exemption chain, read in the packet: EO:7597 (1937-03-31); each is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote (owner ruling, 2026-10-21), and none revokes, amends or shortens this order. This order itself recites EO 6088's two-year exemption; it continues the same person by a new grant. The OFR disposition note on EO 7597 calls EO 7597 an amendment of this order; the text of EO 7597 amends nothing here. The dossier's machine term leads were read against the text; the operative until-date in the command sentence is the end. @rationale:retirement:statute @rationale:retirement:search @rationale:retirement:inventory

savings.reason: Service performed and compensation earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects of the person's continued employment; the order creates no continuing duty, office or rule after its stated term. A later 'further' exemption of the same person is a new grant under the statute, not a savings clause of this order, and the person's employment after the stated date rests on that later order, not on this one.
